about.heroDescription: AgroYachay was born with a clear goal: to give smallholder farmers the same tools as agribusiness, adapted to isolated highland and jungle areas, real budgets and intermittent connectivity.
problems: Parcels in remote areas the agronomist never reaches
Pests detected too late for lack of continuous monitoring
No knowledge of the real state of the soil and the air
Losses from not knowing the forecast in advance
Purchase decisions without comparing real input prices
No history of activities or costs per parcel

faqs.q: Does the Kit include everything needed to install it?
faqs.a: Yes. It comes with the ESP32, DHT11 and FC-28 sensors, cables and the protective case. You only need a 5V USB power supply (a phone charger).

faqs.q: What happens after the first year?
faqs.a: The hardware is yours forever. The web platform costs S/ 59 from the second year onwards, only if you want to keep using the AI and reporting modules.

faqs.q: Can I use the Free plan without buying the sensor?
faqs.a: Yes. The free plan includes crop management, weather, pest detection and the input calculator. It only lacks real-time IoT monitoring.

faqs.q: How do I receive the Kit?
faqs.a: For now by writing to us directly. We ship across Peru via Olva Courier or Serpost. Delivery time: 3 to 7 working days.

faqs.q: Is the ESP32 firmware open source?
faqs.a: Yes. The code is available and you can compile it yourself if you prefer. The Kit arrives with the firmware already installed and tested.

faqs.q: What payment methods do you accept?
faqs.a: Yape, Plin and bank transfer to BCP/Interbank. We issue an electronic payment receipt.

devices.howToConnect: How do I connect a new ESP32?
connectionSteps: Upload the firmware from the /arduino/agrovision_provisioning/ folder using the Arduino IDE.
Install the required libraries: ArduinoJson 6.x, DHT sensor library (Adafruit).
Power on the ESP32. It will create a WiFi network called "AgroVision-Setup-XXXXXX".
Connect your phone or PC to that network (no password). The portal opens automatically.
Select your WiFi network, enter the password and the server URL, then save.
The device will appear here as "Pending": click Link to assign it.

Maíz.desc: Ancestral Andean crop. The purple maize variety has high nutritional value. A staple of the Puno diet.

Cañihua.name: Cañihua
Cañihua.desc: Hardier than quinoa. Highly nutritious. Grows up to 4500 m.a.s.l., where other crops fail.

Habas.name: Faba Beans
Habas.desc: Nitrogen-fixing legume. Improves soil fertility. Eaten both green and dried.

Oca.name: Oca
Oca.desc: Native Andean tuber with a high oxalate content. Second in importance after the potato.

Olluco.name: Ulluco
Olluco.desc: Highly nutritious Andean tuber. Most of its biomass is water. Important in the highland diet.

Tarwi.name: Tarwi
Tarwi.desc: Legume with a higher protein content than soy. Fixes atmospheric nitrogen. Requires debittering.

Trigo.name: Wheat
Trigo.desc: An important cereal for self-consumption and sale. Requires well-drained soil and neutral pH.

Cebada.name: Barley
Cebada.desc: The cereal best adapted to highland conditions. Used as human and animal food and to make chicha.
